title: Checking a TypedDict at run time

starter.solution.py:
from typing import NotRequired, TypedDict


class Product(TypedDict):
    name: str
    price: float
    tags: list[str]
    discount: NotRequired[float]


def parse_product(data: object) -> Product:
    return data

hints: Check the type first (`isinstance(data, dict)`), then the keys (`set(data) - allowed`), then each field in turn, raising as soon as one fails.
`True` is an `int` in Python, so a "number" check needs `and not isinstance(value, bool)`.
